title: the deliveries query is not scoped to the caller's organization
what_is_wrong: The query filters only on `endpoint_id` taken from the URL path, so any authenticated user can enumerate delivery history (event ids, types, response codes) for any other org's endpoints.

title: signing secrets are generated with `random.choice` instead of a CSPRNG
what_is_wrong: `random` is a seedable Mersenne Twister, so observing a few secrets lets an attacker predict others and forge signatures for other tenants' endpoints.

title: the signature is computed over a different byte string than the body that is sent
what_is_wrong: `sign()` HMACs `json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True)` while `client.post(json=...)` serializes the payload independently (different key order and separators), so a receiver verifying against the raw request body gets a mismatch.

title: the timestamp is not part of the signed message
what_is_wrong: The HMAC covers only the serialized payload, so `X-Acme-Timestamp` is unauthenticated and can be rewritten by anyone replaying a captured request, defeating the five-minute replay window the docs rely on.

title: the unique index on `event_id` alone allows only one delivery row per event
what_is_wrong: `enqueue_for_event` inserts one row per matching endpoint for the same `event_id`, so any org with two or more subscribed endpoints hits a unique-violation and loses every delivery for that event.

title: the CHECK list omits the `failed_permanent` status the code writes
what_is_wrong: The constraint allows `('pending','in_flight','delivered','failed')` but `_finish` writes `"failed_permanent"`, so exhausting retries raises a constraint violation instead of recording the failure.

title: `time.sleep()` blocks the event loop inside an async coroutine
what_is_wrong: The retry backoff calls the synchronous `time.sleep(delay)`, which freezes the whole worker process (all 100 gathered deliveries and the lock refresh) for up to 16 seconds per retry.

title: claimed rows are used after their session closes
what_is_wrong: `session_scope()` commits and expires the ORM instances on exit, so the later reads of `delivery.attempts`, `delivery.payload` and `delivery.id` in `deliver`/`send_once` raise DetachedInstanceError.

title: the endpoint object is read outside the session it was loaded in
what_is_wrong: `session.get(m.WebhookEndpoint, ...)` returns an instance whose session has already exited, so `endpoint.signing_secret` and `endpoint.url` in `send_once` touch expired attributes and fail.

title: the distributed lock is a non-atomic get-then-set
what_is_wrong: Two workers can both see an empty `LOCK_KEY` before either sets it, and the separate `set`/`expire` pair can leave a lock with no TTL if the process dies between them, so the batch is processed twice.

title: rows are claimed without row-level locking
what_is_wrong: The SELECT has no `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and the status flip is a separate write, so two concurrent workers (the redis lock being unreliable) select the same pending rows and deliver each webhook twice.

title: the lock is deleted unconditionally even after it has expired
what_is_wrong: `finally: redis_client.delete(LOCK_KEY)` deletes whatever key is present without checking ownership, so a batch that outruns the 60-second TTL erases the lock a different worker now holds.

title: the lock TTL is far shorter than the work it protects
what_is_wrong: A batch of 100 deliveries with a 30-second request timeout and up to 30 seconds of in-process backoff per delivery routinely exceeds 60 seconds, so the lock lapses mid-batch and a second worker starts.

title: `batch` can be referenced before assignment
what_is_wrong: If `_claim_batch()` raises, the `finally` block runs and control falls through to `if not batch`, raising NameError and killing the worker loop.

title: `asyncio.gather` without `return_exceptions` abandons the rest of the batch
what_is_wrong: The first non-HTTPError exception from any `deliver` (TypeError from a non-serializable payload, AttributeError on a missing row) propagates out of `gather` while sibling tasks are still running, and the `finally` then releases the lock underneath them.

title: rows stay `in_flight` forever when a worker dies mid-retry
what_is_wrong: `_claim_batch` only selects `status == "pending"`, and nothing ever moves `in_flight` rows back, so any crash, deploy or lock expiry during the multi-minute retry loop strands those deliveries permanently.

title: retry state is never persisted between attempts
what_is_wrong: `attempt` is a local counter and `attempts`/`next_attempt_at` are only written once at the terminal `_finish`, so the `next_attempt_at` scheduling column is unused and a restart restarts the attempt count from the stale DB value.

title: 4xx responses are retried instead of failing permanently
what_is_wrong: The success test is `200 <= status < 300` and every other status falls into the retry path, so a 400 or 404 is retried five times, contradicting the documented "a 4xx is permanent and we stop immediately".

title: signed POSTs are followed to redirect targets
what_is_wrong: A customer endpoint can answer 307 with any Location and httpx will re-POST the signed body and secret-derived signature headers to that host, including internal addresses.

title: the destination URL is not checked against internal networks
what_is_wrong: Any authenticated user can register `http://127.0.0.1:...` or `http://169.254.169.254/...` and the worker will POST to it from inside the network, giving a full SSRF primitive.

title: `scheme.startswith("http")` accepts plain http and bogus schemes
what_is_wrong: The check passes for `http://`, contradicting the docs' "Only `https://` URLs are accepted", and also for anything else beginning with those four characters such as `httpfoo://`.

title: `signing_secret` is returned by the list endpoint as well as creation
what_is_wrong: `to_dict()` always includes the secret and `list_webhook_endpoints` returns it for every endpoint, so the secret is readable on demand by any org member, contradicting the documented "it cannot be read back afterwards".

title: a failed enqueue is swallowed and the webhook is lost forever
what_is_wrong: The event row is already committed when `enqueue_for_event` runs in its own transaction, and its failure is only logged at warning level with no outbox or retry, so the documented at-least-once guarantee does not hold.

title: an exception from an in-process subscriber prevents webhook enqueue
what_is_wrong: `await subscriber(envelope)` runs before the webhook block and is unguarded, so one failing subscriber silently drops the outbound webhook for an event that was already persisted.

title: the hardcoded allowlist contradicts the documented "every event type we emit"
what_is_wrong: Only three types can ever reach the webhook path, so an endpoint registered with empty `event_types` receives nothing for any other event the system emits.

title: the signature comparison is not constant time
what_is_wrong: `expected == signature` short-circuits on the first differing byte, leaking timing information to a caller probing signatures — while the docs instruct customers to use a constant-time comparison.

title: `next_attempt_at` is set with naive `datetime.utcnow()`
what_is_wrong: The value has no tzinfo while `_claim_batch` compares against a tz-aware `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`, so the comparison depends on the driver's coercion and can mis-order or exclude rows.

title: column types disagree on timezone
what_is_wrong: The ORM declares `DateTime(timezone=True)` while the migration creates plain `TIMESTAMP` columns defaulted with `now()`, so offsets are dropped and DB-side defaults record server-local time.

title: `session.get` result is used without a None check
what_is_wrong: If the delivery row was deleted (for example by the endpoint's ON DELETE CASCADE), `row.status = status` raises AttributeError on None and the delivery is left `in_flight`.

title: a missing endpoint row is not handled
what_is_wrong: `session.get(m.WebhookEndpoint, delivery.endpoint_id)` can return None for a deleted endpoint, and `send_once` then dereferences `endpoint.signing_secret`, raising inside the loop rather than failing the delivery.

title: the endpoint's `active` flag is not rechecked at send time
what_is_wrong: Only `enqueue_for_event` filters on `active`, so a delivery already queued keeps being retried for minutes after a customer deactivates the endpoint.

title: signature and timestamp headers are logged at info level
what_is_wrong: `log.info("POST %s headers=%s", endpoint.url, headers)` writes the full header dict, putting per-request authentication material and the customer URL into shipped logs.

title: the remote response body is stored untruncated
what_is_wrong: `response.text` from an untrusted endpoint goes straight into `response_body`, so a customer can push arbitrarily large content into the database on every attempt.

title: the test never verifies the signature against the body it captured
what_is_wrong: It only asserts the header starts with `sha256=` and is 64 hex chars, so the serialization mismatch between `sign()` and the httpx-encoded body passes the test that claims to cover signed posting.

title: the retry loop, claiming, locking and enqueue paths have no tests
what_is_wrong: Only the pure helpers and `send_once` are exercised, so `deliver`, `_finish`, `_claim_batch`, `_acquire_lock`, `run_worker` and `enqueue_for_event` — where every state transition lives — are entirely uncovered.

title: the delivered request contains no event id
what_is_wrong: `send_once` posts `delivery.payload` (the raw event payload) with no envelope and no id header, so a consumer has nothing to deduplicate on.

title: the documented jitter does not exist
what_is_wrong: `backoff_for` returns exactly `2**attempt` seconds, so all endpoints retry in lockstep after an outage rather than with the documented jitter.

title: `limit` has a lower bound but no upper bound
what_is_wrong: `Query(50, ge=1)` lets a caller pass `limit=10000000`, so a single request can pull an unbounded result set out of the deliveries table.

title: the new flag is never read by any code in the change
what_is_wrong: The migration adds `webhooks_enabled BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE`, but neither the dispatcher nor `enqueue_for_event` consults it, so webhooks fire for orgs the column says are disabled.

title: `event_types` values are not validated against known event types
what_is_wrong: Any string is accepted and stored, so a typo like `invoice.payed` silently subscribes the endpoint to an event that will never fire.

title: the request model accepts unknown fields
what_is_wrong: `BaseModel` without `extra="forbid"` silently ignores extra keys, so a client typo in a field name is accepted with a 201 and different behaviour than requested.

title: no bound on endpoint count, URL length or `event_types` size
what_is_wrong: Nothing limits how many endpoints an org registers or how large the stored URL and JSONB list are, so a single caller can grow the table and the per-event fan-out without limit.

title: batch concurrency is unbounded and untimed as a whole
what_is_wrong: `asyncio.gather` fires all 100 claimed deliveries at once with no semaphore and no overall deadline, so a slow set of endpoints holds 100 sockets for 30 seconds each per attempt.

title: synchronous DB work runs inside async functions
what_is_wrong: `session_scope()` is a blocking context manager called from coroutines, so every query stalls the event loop that the delivery tasks share.

title: the webhook enqueue catches bare `Exception`
what_is_wrong: Any programming error inside `enqueue_for_event` — a TypeError, a bad attribute — is downgraded to a warning line, hiding real bugs behind what looks like a transient delivery problem.

title: the status tuple is declared but never enforced
what_is_wrong: Nothing validates writes against `STATUSES`, and it also disagrees with the migration's CHECK list, so it documents a contract no code applies.

title: `updated_at` has no `onupdate`
what_is_wrong: It is only refreshed where `_finish` sets it by hand, so any other write to the row leaves a stale timestamp.

title: the index does not match the claim query
what_is_wrong: `_claim_batch` filters on `status` and `next_attempt_at` and orders by `next_attempt_at`, but only `status` is indexed, so the queue scan sorts a large low-cardinality bucket on every poll.

title: no index on `org_id`
what_is_wrong: Both `list_webhook_endpoints` and `enqueue_for_event` filter on `org_id`, which is only a foreign key and gets no index in Postgres by default.

title: `event_id` has no foreign key to the events table
what_is_wrong: The column is a bare BIGINT while every other id here is a real reference, so delivery rows can outlive or never match an event.

title: the migration has no down/rollback path
what_is_wrong: Only the forward `BEGIN … COMMIT` block exists, so reverting the release requires hand-written SQL to drop the two tables and the `organizations` column.

title: the constant names bytes but is used as a character count
what_is_wrong: `SECRET_BYTES = 32` is fed to `range()` over an alphanumeric alphabet, so it produces 32 characters, and the test asserting `len(secret) == prefix + SECRET_BYTES` locks in the misnamed semantics.

title: `verify` takes no timestamp and cannot enforce freshness
what_is_wrong: Its signature accepts only secret, payload and signature, so the replay window the docs require of consumers cannot be implemented with the helper the project ships.

title: the shared secret is stored in plaintext
what_is_wrong: The column is a plain `TEXT` with no encryption or hashing, so a read-only database compromise yields every customer's signing key.

title: the test asserts a constant against a literal
what_is_wrong: `assert MAX_ATTEMPTS == 5` cannot fail for the reason its name claims, because it never exercises that five attempts are actually made.

title: the test pins the undocumented no-jitter behaviour
what_is_wrong: It asserts exact equality with 2, 4, 8, 16 seconds, so the documented jitter can never be added without the test failing, and attempt 0 and attempt 5 are untested.

title: hand-rolled fakes stand in for the project's own ORM models
what_is_wrong: Class-attribute stubs never expire or detach, so the detached-instance behaviour that breaks `deliver` in production is invisible to the suite.

title: the new HTTP routes have no tests
what_is_wrong: Nothing covers URL rejection, the 201 body, or org scoping of `list_deliveries`, so the API surface added by this change is unverified.

title: the secret test checks only shape
what_is_wrong: It asserts prefix and length, which a predictable `random`-based generator satisfies exactly as well as a CSPRNG one.

title: no role check on a settings-mutating route
what_is_wrong: `current_user` only establishes identity, so any member of an org can register a destination that receives all of that org's invoice and subscription events.
